title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

errors: No mathematical errors on this page. All moment arms and signs check out: 2aB + Maθ = Ca; A, B = ½C ± ½Mθ; ½aC + Maθ = 2Eeθ, which agrees with the lower-arm check on the next page.

Minor logical point: the claim that equilibrium of moments about one axis implies it about all axes requires the resultant force to vanish. Euler has already imposed this, so the statement is correct in context but stated without that qualifier.
The model neglects the vertical compressive force transmitted through the hinge in its treatment of the spring. This is consistent to first order in θ.

ideas.what: Static equilibrium via force balance plus moment balance about a convenient point, then the free-body diagram of one arm about the hinge
ideas.where_published: Many Euler mechanics papers; E510 itself

ideas.what: Column modeled as two rigid bars joined by a rotational elastic spring, loaded by its own weight; leads to a linear equilibrium equation whose coefficient vanishes at a critical weight
ideas.modern_name: Discrete rigid-link/spring buckling model (Hencky bar-chain type); self-weight buckling (Greenhill problem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hencky (1920s) for bar-chain discretization; Greenhill (1881) for self-weight column; Euler for column buckling (1744, 1778 papers E508–E510)
ideas.where_published: E510 (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778:I, publ. 1780); discussed in Truesdell's Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11/2) — extent of discussion of this discrete model: unsure

ideas.what: Spring moment taken as stiffness times relative rotation 2θ of the two arms
ideas.modern_name: Linear rotational spring / lumped bending stiffness
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler / Jacob Bernoulli (moment proportional to curvature)
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum de curvis elasticis (1744), E510

missed.claim: Euler's two-link spring model of a self-weight column is an early instance of the lumped-parameter bar-chain discretization of an elastic column, usually associated with Hencky (1920s). It is unclear whether historians explicitly connect E510's discrete model to later discrete stability models.
missed.quote: nostrum systema in puncto C fixum concipiamus, cuius ergo respectu vires, quae brachium C A seorsim sollicitant, se mutuo in aequilibrio seruare debent
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is only a minor historiographical priority point for discrete stability models. The model itself is elementary and probably known to Truesdell's commentary.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, routine statics for a discrete two-bar buckling model. The model is known as part of E510 and is likely discussed in Truesdell's history. At most a slight priority note for the bar-chain discretization idea.
transcription_corrections: 'pynctum' in the scan should read 'punctum' (the transcription already normalizes this).
Transcription otherwise matches the image; the long s and the italic a/θ are rendered correctly.
